items.stem: A student pays the tuition for three enlisted courses. Looking at the part where the money moves, which choice names the resource, the event and the agents?

options.text: Resource: the amount paid. Event: the payment. Agents: the student and the university.
options.feedback: The resource is the thing of value, the event records that it changed hands, and the agents are the people or organizations on each side.

options.text: Resource: the student. Event: the amount paid. Agents: the payment.
options.feedback: These roles are mixed up. The student is an agent, and the thing of value is the resource.

options.text: Resource: the payment. Event: the amount paid. Agents: the student.
options.feedback: The payment is the event, because it records something that happened. The amount is what changed hands.

options.text: Resource: a seat in a course. Event: the payment. Agents: the university only.
options.feedback: The seat is the resource in the enlistment half of the pair. In the payment half the resource is the money, and the student is an agent too.

items.stem: Maria pays ₱18,000 in one transfer for three subjects. Juan pays the ₱7,500 for one subject in two installments. Why does the model need a separate allocations table that links payments and enlistments?

options.text: One payment can cover many enlistments, and one enlistment can have many payments.
options.feedback: A pairing that is many-to-many needs its own table, and the amount applied to each enlistment can be stored only there.

options.text: Banking rules require payments to be kept in a table of their own.
options.feedback: The reason comes from the shape of the data, not from banking rules.

options.text: A separate table makes the payments table faster to search and back up.
options.feedback: Speed is not the reason. Without the allocations table you could not store installments or shared transfers at all.

options.text: Each enlistment should always have exactly one payment, so the table is optional.
options.feedback: That holds only until the first student pays in installments or one transfer covers several subjects.

items.stem: A school records each enlistment and each payment as separate events. Which question needs both kinds of event to answer?

options.text: Which students hold a seat and have not paid?
options.feedback: This question looks for a gap between two events that should pair up, an enlistment with no matching payment.

options.text: How many seats does MGT 45 have in total?
options.feedback: This needs only the resource, the seats. No event is involved.

options.text: Which room is MGT 45 held in this term?
options.feedback: This is a fact about the course and its room. It needs no payment.

options.text: What is Maria's student number on record?
options.feedback: This is an attribute of one student and needs neither event.
